content.text: The docs currently overstate two things: copying `OUT_DIR` applies to Rust compilations, while C/C++ only gets path remapping; and the cached files are read-only, but their directories remain writable. I’m clarifying those details, adding a concrete example and fallback conditions, and preserving the old section link.

The copy is read-only, so a compilation that writes into `OUT_DIR` -fails rather than altering what other checkouts read. - -Three cases stay checkout-specific. A build script that writes the checkout's -path into its output produces different bytes in each checkout, so the copies -differ and the crate compiles once per checkout. A crate that reads `OUT_DIR` -only through a source outside its own directory, which the scan does not see, -compiles with the value Cargo gave it. This includes crates that load generated code: + +```rust +include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs")); +``` + +Cargo normally places `OUT_DIR` under each checkout's target directory. That +path becomes a cache-key input when a crate reads it, causing a miss in a new +checkout even if `generated.rs` is identical. mbx copies the output to +`out-dirs/v1/` under its cache and gives rustc that shared path as +`OUT_DIR`. Matching output trees therefore use the same path and can +reuse the compilation when its other inputs also match. + +The literal `OUT_DIR` value remains part of the key. text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/pr498-tools.xnoetu/pr-body.md
+Rust crates that read `OUT_DIR` can now reuse cached compilations across checkouts when their build-script output and other compilation inputs match. Previously, the checkout-specific `OUT_DIR` value caused a cache miss even when the generated files were identical.
+
+For example, a crate that includes generated Rust code can reuse its artifact in a second worktree:
+
+```rust
+include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"));
+```
+
+mbx copies eligible build-script output to `out-dirs/v1/<digest>` under its cache and supplies that path to rustc as `OUT_DIR`. Matching output trees give rustc the same path, including when code stores or derives a value from it. The literal path remains part of the cache key; different output trees use different keys.
+
+### Configuration and compatibility
+
+- Enabled by default through `share_out_dir`. Use `MBX_SHARE_OUT_DIR=0 mbx build` or `share_out_dir = false` in `.mbx.toml` to preserve Cargo's original `OUT_DIR` and generated source paths.
+- Sharing requires a detectable `OUT_DIR` reference and output mbx can copy. Missed references, unsupported output such as symlinks, and copy failures retain Cargo's original directory. Reuse across machines also requires matching absolute cache paths.
+- Cached files are marked read-only. Code that modifies generated output during compilation should disable sharing. Build scripts still produce their output in Cargo's original directory.
+- `mbx cache stats` reports copies as **generated source trees**. Automatic collection and `mbx gc` age them using `target.max_age`; a later compilation recreates an evicted copy. Embedded `OUT_DIR` paths are not permanent runtime storage.
+- The setting also controls generated source path remapping in Rust and C/C++ debug information. The shared directory is supplied to Rust compilations; C/C++ continues to use the original build-script output directory.
+
+### Validation
+
+Integration coverage checks reuse across two checkouts, different generated output, dependent-crate reuse, and Cargo freshness after restoration. Unit coverage checks tree identity, executable bits, symlink fallback, read-only file permissions, source scanning, and age-based collection.
+
+<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
+https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mr-boxington/trails/10
+<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->
*** End Patch"));
